issues.description: The SHACL shape for ships does not enforce the activation condition that the requirement applies only to Polar‑Class ships (i.e., when `nltl:polarClassRequirementsApplicable` is true). Consequently the shape validates every ship instance, which deviates from the represented requirement that the corrosion/abrasion addition of 1.0 mm is mandatory only for Polar‑Class ships.
issues.suggestion: Add a property constraint to `_:ShipCorrosionAbrasionAdditionShape` that checks `nltl:polarClassRequirementsApplicable` has the literal value `true` (xsd:boolean). This will restrict the validation to ships for which the Polar‑Class applicability flag is set.

questions.missing: Activation condition for Polar‑Class applicability (value of `nltl:polarClassRequirementsApplicable`)
questions.why: The regulation states the corrosion/abrasion addition applies only to Polar‑Class ships. The current SHACL applies the constraint to all ships, which may cause false‑positive validation failures for non‑Polar‑Class vessels.

change_review.reason: Removal of several path‑logic constraints reduced the expressiveness of the model and eliminated checks that helped ensure the correct traversal of internal structures. This regression may allow malformed graphs to pass validation.

The removal of the target‑applicability condition (`nltl:polarClassRequirementsApplicable`) means the ship shape now validates every ship, contrary to the requirement that it applies only to Polar‑Class ships.
Removing the `sh:targetClass qudt:QuantityValue` from `_:QuantityValueShape` broadens the shape’s applicability to any node, which could lead to unintended validation of non‑quantity nodes.
